title: The Massacre at Tiananmen Square
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a note recorded in June 2020 about George Floyd, Black Lives Matter, and the relevance of the topic, then cover the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre in Beijing. They trace the lead-up from the death of reformist leader Hu Yaobang in April 1989, the student-led memorial and sit-in, the People's Daily editorial, the hunger strike during Gorbachev's visit, martial law, the army's first incursion blocked by Beijing residents, the second deadly assault on June 3-4, the students' withdrawal from the square, and the Western journalist footage on Chang'an Avenue. They discuss the death toll estimates, the Tank Man photo taken by Charlie Cole and his fate, the government's economic reform trade-off, and close with a listener mail about pandemic flu predictions.
topics: non-violent resistance Beijing suburbs army convoy

segments.title: Opening remarks and introduction
segments.summary: The hosts record a note about George Floyd and Black Lives Matter, then open the show with banter and introduce the topic of Tank Man and the Tiananmen Square massacre.

segments.title: Background: student reform movement and Hu Yaobang
segments.summary: The hosts describe the late 1980s push by students for anti-corruption measures and free speech, the reformist leader Hu Yaobang who was forced out in 1987 and died April 15, 1989, and the power split in the Communist Party between Deng Xiaoping and Zhao Ziyang.

segments.title: Memorial turns into Tiananmen sit-in
segments.summary: Thousands of students gathered in Tiananmen Square for Hu Yaobang's memorial and stayed to hold speeches and demand political reform, largely from Beijing University. The hosts discuss Li Peng as the hardline antagonist and Zhao Ziyang's more sympathetic stance.

segments.title: People's Daily editorial and escalation
segments.summary: While Zhao Ziyang was out of the country, the People's Daily ran an editorial denouncing the demonstrations, which backfired and spread protests to some 400 cities. The hosts note the shift when ordinary workers joined, and the hunger strike timed to Gorbachev's visit.

segments.title: Martial law and army convoys blocked by residents
segments.summary: Martial law was called for and a large protest followed. The army sent around 300,000 troops toward Beijing, but residents of the suburbs surrounded the convoys, brought food and drink, and talked with soldiers, and the troops eventually withdrew after about four days.
topics: non-violent resistance Beijing suburbs army convoy

segments.title: Second assault and the June 3-4 killings
segments.summary: The government sent troops again with authorization for deadly force. On the night of June 3 the army advanced and opened fire, then shot at people fleeing. The hosts describe the reported sniper shootings and an account by Sir Alan Donald.

segments.title: Students leave the square and Chang'an Avenue violence
segments.summary: Around 1:30 am the army reached the square and the student leadership voted to leave after being given an ultimatum. The hosts then describe the bloodiest fighting on June 4 on Chang'an Avenue, where Western journalists in a hotel recorded events, including attacks on ambulances.

segments.title: Death toll, Tank Man, and Charlie Cole's photograph
segments.summary: The hosts discuss casualty estimates, including a claim of at least 10,000 killed and the Chinese government's lower figure. They describe June 5, when a lone man stood in front of a column of tanks on Chang'an Avenue, and how photographer Charlie Cole hid his film in a toilet tank, with the image spreading worldwide.

segments.title: Tank Man's fate, aftermath, and economic trade-off
segments.summary: The hosts discuss uncertainty about what happened to Tank Man, the Victory film comparison, the Eastern European protests that the image inspired, and the government's shift to economic reform and foreign investment in exchange for no political reform. They note the imprisoned count from the Dui Hua Foundation.

segments.title: Listener mail on pandemic flu
segments.summary: The hosts read a listener mail from Tiffany about being in lockdown in Oregon, and play a clip of a 2017 listener mail about the risk of a flu pandemic and CDC funding.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and give the email address for contacting the show.
